sections.h2: Register of Deeds address and phone
sections.html:
Go to 155 N. Ocoee Street, Suite 102, Cleveland, TN 37311, or call 423-728-7240. Tennessee records land by county, so a deed for any house in Bradley County is filed at this one office, whether the property sits in Cleveland, in Charleston or in the unincorporated hills between them.

Call before you drive over with a deed, and ask for the total recording charge for your page count and for the office's hours that day.

An estimated 115,465 people lived in Bradley County in July 2025, in 47,861 housing units. Owners occupy 67.3 percent of homes, and the median owner-occupied value is $261,900 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $1,030, which a landlord should weigh when deciding between selling and holding. Cleveland is the county seat and largest city, and Charleston is the other city. Public schools are split between Bradley County Schools and Cleveland City Schools.

Ridges run through the county, and Candies Creek Ridge crosses Cleveland. A lot on a slope needs a careful survey and drainage check before a buyer's lender signs off.

The county directs searchers to TitleSearcher, a vendor site that gives online access to land records around the clock. Its images and index data cover deeds, mortgages, releases, powers of attorney, restrictions, plat maps and other document types filed at the register's office.

The register's page also links a property fraud alert sign-up. Alerts watch for new filings under your name, which helps if you own a rental, inherited land or a vacant lot you seldom visit. A forger working against an empty house is counting on the owner not noticing.

Before listing, pull the vesting deed for your parcel and check three things: the spelling of every owner name, the legal description, and any deed of trust that was never released. A lender that was paid off but never filed a release leaves a cloud on the title, and a closing agent will ask you to clear it.

sections.h2: Taxes due when a deed is recorded
sections.html:
State law sets these taxes, and they are the same in every Tennessee county. The Department of Revenue lists a realty transfer tax of $0.37 per $100 and a mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 of indebtedness, with the first $2,000 of the debt exempt.

Charge or ruleHow it works
Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100 of the greater of price or value
Who pays itThe grantee (buyer) named on the deed
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100 of debt, first $2,000 exempt, paid by the borrower
Required statement on debt instrumentsMaximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes
Register receipt feeUp to $1 per receipt for each tax
Penalty for unpaid indebtedness tax$250 or double the unpaid tax, whichever is greater

Ask the title agent for the exact charge on your deal before closing.

The state manual excludes a short list of transfers. Several come up in estates, divorces and family moves, where an owner may need to sell quickly.

  • Deeds an executor signs to carry out a devise in a will.
  • Domestic settlement decrees and deeds that adjust property rights between divorcing parties.
  • A conveyance from one spouse to the other that creates or dissolves a tenancy by the entirety.
  • Transfers into a revocable living trust by the person who made it, and transfers back to that person or the spouse.
  • Real estate formerly held by tenants in common, and the release of a life estate to the remainder beneficiaries.
  • Transfers to or from a government entity.

No oath of consideration is needed on an exempt transfer. On a taxable deed, the buyer swears to the price or value on the face of the deed in front of the register, and the state can compare that figure with the assessor's value later.

When unrelated parties trade, the price paid is the usual figure. Where value drives the tax, the state accepts the tax base at the local assessor's office, or a recent appraisal the assessor has accepted, as fair market value. A lower figure can be audited and assessed with penalties and interest.

The Bradley County Assessor of Property is at the Courthouse Annex, 155 Broad Street NW, Room 105, phone 423-728-7125. The office runs a Tennessee property viewer for parcel data and tax maps. Look up the assessor's number for your house before you sign a deed that states a value far from it.

sections.h2: State rules that affect your deed
sections.html:
The Department of Revenue manual sets several rules that the register applies at the counter. Knowing them ahead of time keeps a closing from stalling on a technicality.

  • A person who obtains several deeds for the same tract in one transfer pays the transfer tax only once, and no tax is due until title passes by deed.
  • A modified or amended deed or deed of trust should carry the book and page of the earlier document, so the register can see that tax was already paid.
  • Every instrument that evidences debt must state the maximum principal indebtedness, and the register may not record it until that statement is supplied and the tax is paid.
  • An assumption agreement where the buyer promises to pay the debt while the seller stays liable creates no new debt, so no mortgage tax is due. A new contract that cancels the seller's obligation does create new debt and is taxed.
  • Tax paid in another jurisdiction is proved by naming that jurisdiction and giving the book and page of the recorded document.

If your house has a payoff, ask the lender how and when it will file the release of its deed of trust. The release is what clears the record, and a buyer's title agent will look for it.

sections.h2: Selling a Bradley County house for cash
sections.html:
A cash sale keeps recording simple. We buy Bradley County houses as-is, and the deed is recorded here like any other. With no lender there is no deed of trust, so no mortgage tax applies. The buyer still owes the transfer tax and swears to the value.

Bring the previous deed, your tax bill and any payoff figures. If a deed has an error, the register records documents as presented, so ask the title company or attorney who drafted it how to correct it, and call 423-728-7240 to confirm what the office needs to accept the corrected version.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Bradley County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 155 N. Ocoee Street, Suite 102, Cleveland, TN 37311. The phone is 423-728-7240.

faqs.q: Can I search Bradley County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes. The county directs people to TitleSearcher, which offers land record images and index data around the clock. The register's page also links a property fraud alert sign-up.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax in Bradley County?
faqs.a: $0.37 per $100 of the price or value, the same in every Tennessee county. The buyer named on the deed owes it, and the register collects it at recording.

faqs.q: Do I pay mortgage tax if I sell for cash?
faqs.a: No. Mortgage tax is $0.115 per $100 of debt above the first $2,000 and applies to instruments such as a deed of trust. A cash purchase has no deed of trust.

faqs.q: Does the register fix errors in my deed?
faqs.a: The register records documents as they are presented. Ask the title company or attorney who drafted the deed how to correct it, and call 423-728-7240 to confirm what the office needs.
